papers.title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks several popular general-purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks that require both writing code and multi-step reasoning. It finds that while LLMs show promise for automating computational biology workflows, their performance varies and they are not yet fully reliable on these tasks. The work provides an assessment framework for evaluating AI agents in bioinformatics.

papers.title: XChrom: A Cross-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Prediction Model Integrating Genomic Sequence and Cellular Context.
papers.abstract: Single-cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single-cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outper
papers.summary: XChrom is a deep learning framework that predicts single-cell chromatin accessibility genome-wide by combining genomic sequence with cell identity information derived from single-cell transcriptomics. It is designed to predict accessibility for both unseen genomic regions and unseen cells, addressing a gap in existing computational models. Comprehensive evaluations show it consistently outperforms prior approaches.

papers.title: pdb2reaction: End-to-End Reaction-Path Elucidation from PDB Structures Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials.
papers.abstract: Elucidating enzymatic reaction mechanisms requires a sequence of computational tasks comprising active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state (TS) refinement, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation, and quasi-rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (QRRHO) thermochemistrystages typically connected by ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning. We present pdb2reaction, an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates this entire pipeline directly from a user-curated PDB using a single machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) backend. A GPU-accelerated pysisyphu
papers.summary: pdb2reaction is an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates the full enzymatic reaction-mechanism workflow—active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state refinement, IRC validation, and QRRHO thermochemistry—starting directly from a user-curated PDB file. It uses a single machine-learning interatomic potential backend with GPU acceleration, replacing the ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning typically needed to connect these stages.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare und
papers.summary: This paper introduces a resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and a controlled evaluation protocol for deep-learning-based segmentation of protein secondary structures in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. It systematically compares volumetric segmentation architectures across finer resolution ranges, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation in this regime. The work aims to clarify how segmentation performance degrades with resolution and which architectures perform best.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that converts literature on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable evidence records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and auditable.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Augmented Stimulated Raman Imaging for Cell-Type-Specific Metabolic Profiling in Live Neuronal Cocultures.
papers.abstract: Neuronal metabolism is fundamental to brain functions and diseases, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics and interactions remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a tandem deep-learning approach integrated with bioorthogonal chemical imaging using stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy. This method achieves high-speed and quantitative metabolic profiling in live neuronal cocultures. Our deep-learning framework consists of a recurrent convolutional neural network (RCNN) that enables high-resolution 3D imaging with minimal photodamage and a U-Net segmentation model for cell-type-speci
papers.summary: This paper presents a tandem deep-learning framework combined with stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy to enable high-speed, quantitative metabolic profiling in live neuronal cocultures. A recurrent convolutional network achieves high-resolution 3D imaging with minimal photodamage, while a U-Net model segments cell types for cell-type-specific metabolic readouts. The approach enables spatially and temporally resolved study of neuronal metabolism in live systems.

papers.title: Prediction of Residue-Level Base Preference for DNA-Binding Proteins Using a Multimodal Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: Specific recognition between proteins and DNA governs essential cellular functions, yet the binding specificity of most DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) remains experimentally uncharacterized and high-throughput experimental methods still lag far behind the ever-growing protein data set. Here, we present 3M-BSIP (3-modal base-specific interaction predictor), a multimodal deep learning framework capable of predicting the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DBPs. 3M-BSIP constructs a holistic protein representation by integrating three distinct modalities: a protein language m
papers.summary: The authors present 3M-BSIP, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DNA-binding proteins. It integrates three protein representation modalities, including a protein language model, to address the gap between the growing number of known proteins and the limited experimentally characterized DNA-binding specificities. This offers a computational route to annotate binding specificity for the many DBPs lacking experimental data.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion
papers.summary: The authors present AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework that uses a large language model to guide parallel, multi-site sequence editing of therapeutic antibodies, optimizing several properties simultaneously. The method identifies which positions to edit and what edits to make (including keeping, substituting, inserting, or deleting residues), addressing the vast sequence space and sparse annotations that make joint optimization difficult.

papers.title: [pMHCBind: predicting major histocompatibility complex class I-peptide interactions via protein large language models and hypergraph neural networks].
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules initiate CD8+ T cell immune responses by presenting antigenic peptides, a process fundamentally governed by the spatial interaction network mediated by multi-residue synergy between the binding groove and the peptide. Accurate modeling of this mechanism is crucial for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy. However, existing methods are largely confined to sequence-level modeling, failing to capture cross-residue higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained binding interface interactions. To address these ch
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The authors present pMHCBind, a computational method that combines protein large language models with hypergraph neural networks to predict whether antigenic peptides bind MHC class I molecules. By modeling higher-order structural dependencies between peptide residues and the MHC binding groove rather than relying only on sequence, the approach aims to improve neoantigen screening for cancer immunotherapy. The work is a methodological contribution to peptide-MHC binding prediction.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study used high-resolution 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 carefully designed sentences to test whether transformer-based language models represent sentence meaning like the human brain. By disentangling sentence structure from word meaning and comparing eight transformers with eleven other models via representational similarity analysis, the authors found that LLMs poorly capture how word order shapes neural representations of meaning. The work suggests current language models diverge from human brain processing of syntax and compositional semantics.

papers.title: BioHarness: Substrate-Aware Evidence Assembly for Biomedical Question Answering across Literature, Knowledge Bases, and Biological Atlases.
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assemble
papers.summary: BioHarness introduces a substrate-aware LLM framework for biomedical question answering that dynamically decides when to rely on retrieved literature, when to resolve gene aliases and database identifiers, and when to execute queries over structured biological atlases. This selective evidence assembly aims to overcome the fixed workflows of standard RAG systems, improving answer accuracy by invoking the right evidence source at the right time.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors present EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph features to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They build the model on PDBbind v2020.R1 and reduce sequence-homology leakage by clustering receptor and ligand sequences independently before splitting. The approach targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting amyloidogenic sequences to structural biology and inhibitor/drug design for diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It organizes the field into key application domains and evaluates the methods used in each.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportuniti
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing use of Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy (Raman, IR, NIR, SERS) for tasks such as spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. It highlights how Transformer architectures capture long-range dependencies in spectral data and enable applications across chemistry, biology, and materials science.

papers.title: A multimodal deep learning model for classifying early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on biparametric MRI.
papers.abstract: Precise early- versus late-stage stratification of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is critical for hip-preserving treatment selection, yet conventional MRI interpretation suffers from interobserver variability and limited objectivity. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning model integrating biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE) with clinical parameters (including age, sex, affected side (left, right, or bilateral), and etiology) to differentiate early- from late-stage ONFH and provide objective imaging evidence.
papers.summary: This study developed a multimodal deep learning model that combines biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE sequences) with clinical parameters such as age, sex, affected side, and etiology to classify early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head. The goal is to provide objective imaging evidence that reduces interobserver variability in staging, which is critical for deciding on hip-preserving treatment. The abstract describes the model's development and aims but does not report performance results.

papers.title: AIDCare: A Technical Proof-of-Concept for Integrating Personalized Nutrition, Physical Activity, and AI-Assisted Care in Diabetes Lifestyle Management.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical nutrition therapy and structured lifestyle self-management are fundamental to diabetes care, yet conventional mobile health tools typically track diet, physical activity, and glucose measurements in isolation, with limited connection to clinical oversight. This study presents AIDCare, an integrated mobile health platform that connects camera-based nutritional assessment, wearable physical activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and clinician-supervised conversational artificial intelligence (AI) to support personalized dietary and lifestyle self-management i
papers.summary: AIDCare is a proof-of-concept mobile health platform that combines camera-based food recognition, wearable activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and a clinician-supervised conversational AI to support personalized diabetes lifestyle management. The work demonstrates technical integration of these components rather than reporting clinical outcomes, positioning it as an early-stage tool for connecting self-management data with clinical oversight.

papers.title: Use of Demineralized Autologous Dentin Graft with the Tooth Processing Device in Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement and Loading: A 12-Month Evaluation of Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Stability.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of immediate implant placement and loading combined with autologous dentin grafting in reducing post-extraction tissue remodelling, with particular emphasis on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 13 patients (14 implant sites) with Type 1 extraction sockets in the anterior maxilla. Following atraumatic tooth extraction, implants were immediately placed and grafted with autologous dentin processed from the extracted tooth using the Tooth Transformer device. Screw-re
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated 13 patients (14 implant sites) who received immediate dental implants with autologous dentin grafts processed from their own extracted teeth using a dedicated device. Over 12 months, the approach appeared to support peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone, suggesting autologous dentin may help reduce post-extraction tissue remodeling. The small sample and observational design limit the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title: FusionEP: Adaptive Cross-Modal Deep Fusion Network for Essential Protein Identification via Multi-Omics Integration and Contrastive Learning.
papers.abstract: Identifying essential proteins lays a foundation for dissecting disease mechanisms and mining therapeutic targets. Existing algorithms mostly adopt unimodal inputs and struggle to capture multi-level biological interactions from genomics, subcellular localization and proteomics. We present FusionEP, which is an adaptive cross-modal deep fusion network built upon contrastive learning to predict essential proteins. FusionEP integrates gene expression profiles, subcellular localization features, and protein interaction map structures. For gene expression information, we design a six-layer Transfo
papers.summary: FusionEP is a deep learning method that predicts essential proteins by combining gene expression, subcellular localization, and protein-protein interaction data using an adaptive cross-modal fusion network with contrastive learning. It outperforms existing unimodal approaches by capturing multi-level biological interactions across omics layers. The work is aimed at identifying disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Wavelet Scattering Features for Robust Subject-Independent EMG-Based Speech Recognition: A Comparative Analysis.
papers.abstract: Electromyography (EMG)-based speech recognition provides a non-acoustic alternative in high-noise environments and serves as a prospective foundation for assistive technologies for users with speech impairments. While prior work has largely focused on model architecture, the impact of EMG feature representations on the robustness and subject-independent generalization of deep learning models remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how feature representation influences subject-independent EMG speech recognition by comparing two feature extraction pipelines-a conventional Mel-Frequ
papers.summary: This study compares two feature extraction pipelines for EMG-based speech recognition, contrasting conventional Mel-frequency features with wavelet scattering features, to assess how representation choice affects subject-independent generalization in deep learning models. The work highlights that feature design, not just model architecture, plays a key role in robustness and cross-subject performance for non-acoustic speech interfaces.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research.
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Ado
papers.summary: This review argues that artificial intelligence is shifting protein glycosylation research from prediction to generation, addressing three persistent bottlenecks: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of glycan occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. It surveys how AI methods can model the template-free, competition-driven nature of glycan assembly and help reconstruct the field's research paradigm.

papers.title: Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Learning for miRNA-Drug Response Association Prediction Under Cold-Start Generalization.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Cancer drug resistance can be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which can alter gene expression and cellular pathways that determine how cancer cells respond to treatment. Potential miRNA-drug response associations can be identified using computational models; however, evaluating these models using edge-based evaluation can result in an optimistic view of model generalization since test miRNAs or drugs can appear in other response associations during training. (2) Methods: This paper presents a relation-aware heterogeneous learning framework that integrates miRNA expression pro
papers.summary: The paper introduces a relation-aware heterogeneous graph learning framework to predict associations between miRNAs and drug responses, addressing the problem of overly optimistic evaluation in existing computational models. By using cold-start generalization evaluation, where test miRNAs or drugs are entirely unseen during training, the method aims to provide a more realistic assessment of predictive performance. This work is relevant to computational drug discovery and miRNA-based cancer research.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrates 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum depletion as a key microbial signature in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link these changes to hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling and validate the therapeutic potential of can (likely a compound or intervention) in this context.

papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
papers.abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoni
papers.summary: ARGUS is a framework for interpreting noncoding single nucleotide variants that separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-based reasoning, aiming to reduce hallucinations such as fabricated transcription factor binding changes and unsupported experimental evidence. It addresses the major challenge that over 90% of GWAS disease-associated variants lie in regulatory regions and are hard to interpret functionally.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets serine/threonine phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders designed with generative language models. This enables selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual proteins in cells, including disordered substrates that are otherwise difficult to target. The approach addresses a long-standing gap in the ability to control phosphatase activity with substrate specificity.

papers.title: Blood Cell Imaging Analysis for Multiple Sclerosis Classification Using Leave-One-Subject-Out Study with Deep Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease whose diagnosis typically relies on resource-intensive and partly invasive procedures such as MRI and spinal fluid analysis. This study explores whether deep learning can identify distinguishing patterns in RBC images associated with MS, aiming to determine whether blood-cell imaging may provide information relevant to understanding the disease. The initial dataset comprised 121 images from 13 independent subjects. To expand the dataset to 1944 images, image augmentation techniques were applied to the training data to increase image var
papers.summary: This study tested whether deep learning applied to red blood cell images could distinguish multiple sclerosis patients from controls, using a leave-one-subject-out cross-validation design on a small dataset of 13 subjects expanded via image augmentation. The work is preliminary and limited by the very small sample size, but it explores whether blood-cell morphology imaging might carry disease-relevant information as a less invasive alternative to MRI and spinal fluid analysis.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns the latent embeddings of ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor–target interactions. By replacing complex deep architectures with a geometric alignment of pretrained embeddings, the approach aims to generalize better to new chemical scaffolds despite limited interaction data. The work positions linear manifold alignment as an interpretable alternative to deep learning for drug-target prediction.

papers.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models.
papers.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstr
papers.summary: This paper presents a reproducible, adaptable workflow that uses large language models to automatically extract species interaction data from ecological literature, addressing the challenge of synthesizing scattered information across hundreds of thousands of papers. The authors demonstrate the approach on real ecological texts, showing that LLM-based NLP can automate a task that traditionally required extensive manual curation.

papers.title: MGP_HNSC32: A H&E Morphology-Derived 32-Gene Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and mult
papers.summary: The authors built a transformer-based model (CTransPath) that predicts gene expression directly from H&E whole-slide images in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, then used these morphology-derived expression predictions to construct a 32-gene prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) via Random Survival Forest. This links tissue morphology to molecular prognosis, offering a potentially interpretable, image-based prognostic tool for HNSC.

papers.title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classif
papers.summary: This application note empirically evaluates genome-aware weak-strong augmentation strategies for semi-supervised learning (FixMatch and FlexMatch) on DNA sequence classification tasks, using a GROVER DNA language model backbone. The authors find that augmentation designs tailored to biological constraints can yield reliable gains over generic perturbations, though the abstract is truncated before reporting specific results. The work provides practical guidance on which augmentation recipes are most effective for pseudo-label-based SSL in genomics.

papers.title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients.
papers.summary: The authors developed an interpretable multimodal deep learning model that combines whole-slide histopathology images with multiparametric MRI to predict, before surgery, which high-grade glioma patients will benefit from adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The model links DNA damage repair signatures to immune characteristics, offering a potential preoperative tool for treatment stratification.

papers.title: Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study.
papers.abstract: The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops an interpretable multimodal machine learning model that combines systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic features to predict progression from acute appendicitis to septic shock. The work aims to enable earlier identification of hemodynamic deterioration by capturing both systemic immune dysregulation and anatomical barrier failure.

papers.title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level.
papers.summary: This ecological study uses machine learning to relate global thyroid cancer incidence to dietary and socioeconomic factors across countries. It finds that dietary patterns and socioeconomic indicators help explain geographic variation in thyroid cancer incidence, suggesting that factors beyond screening contribute to the observed rise. The work highlights the potential of machine learning for hypothesis generation in global cancer epidemiology.

papers.title: Gradient boosting models for gallstone disease classification: A comparative study using demographic and clinical data.
papers.abstract: Gallstone disease is a prevalent gastrointestinal condition with a substantial healthcare burden. While abdominal ultrasonography is the established first-line diagnostic modality, opportunistic risk stratification using routinely collected health parameters remains underexplored. This study evaluated the discriminatory capacity of four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and HistGBM) for classifying gallstone status using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory features. A retrospective clinical dataset of 319 patients (161 gallstone-positive
papers.summary: This study compared four gradient boosting algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, HistGBM) for classifying gallstone disease using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory data from 319 patients. The work evaluates whether routinely collected health parameters can support opportunistic risk stratification as an alternative to ultrasound-based diagnosis. The abstract is truncated, so the specific performance results and best-performing model are not fully reported.

papers.title: Routine Metabolic Laboratory Profile and Time-Stratified Machine-Learning Risk Stratification of Rosacea: A Combined Retrospective-Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Rosacea has been linked with systemic metabolic abnormalities in case-control studies, but most such evidence compares rosacea patients with healthy controls rather than asking which patients within a rosacea population carry the greatest metabolic burden. We aimed to describe the metabolic profile of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and build a time-stratified, outcome-independent machine-learning model ranking which routine metabolic indicators predict metabolic syndrome status.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the metabolic profile of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and develops a time-stratified machine-learning model to identify which routine metabolic indicators best predict metabolic syndrome status within rosacea patients. Rather than comparing rosacea patients to healthy controls, it focuses on stratifying metabolic risk among rosacea patients themselves.

papers.title: A fuzzy-augmented deep learning pipeline for multilingual natural language processing from handwritten script: a Tamil case study.
papers.abstract: Multilingual natural language processing (NLP) from handwritten script is an open artificial intelligence (AI) challenge requiring advances in both pattern recognition and sequence generation. Existing end-to-end pipelines often fail to model the structural uncertainty in complex scripts, particularly the decorative stroke variability in Dravidian writing systems, before passing representations to downstream NLP models. This omission can result in error propagation from the recognition stage into translation. This paper proposes a Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition and Translation (THCRT)
papers.summary: This paper proposes THCRT, a fuzzy-augmented deep learning pipeline for recognizing handwritten Tamil characters and translating them into another language. The key idea is to model structural uncertainty in decorative stroke variability before passing representations to downstream NLP models, reducing error propagation from recognition into translation. It is a case study for multilingual NLP from handwritten Dravidian scripts.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven discovery of antivirals against respiratory RNA viruses must account for the biology of RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) targets, whose ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, metals, and conformational changes. The authors critique common molecular docking biases and propose RdRp-centered benchmarking to make AI predictions more reliable for antiviral discovery.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that uses protein language model embeddings (ESM-2) combined with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The framework is designed to handle the hierarchical structure of enzyme function and class imbalance, aiming to improve annotation accuracy beyond sequence similarity alone. This offers a practical tool for enzyme function prediction from sequence data.

papers.title: Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (IS) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a machine learning model that uses routine clinical chemistry and hematology biomarkers to rapidly distinguish intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke. Such a laboratory-based approach could support faster triage and treatment decisions in acute stroke care without relying on imaging alone.

papers.title: Ordinal measurement invariance of three retained GAEU-1 dimensions in Chilean and Ecuadorian university samples.
papers.abstract: Meaningful cross-national comparisons of self-regulated learning (SRL), motivation, and related learning-regulation constructs require evidence that the measurement model operates comparably across groups. We tested this requirement for three GAEU-1 dimensions previously retained in Chile and Ecuador using the open Version-5 dataset (N = 1,316; Chile n = 631; Ecuador n = 685). Fifteen ordered indicators representing the GAEU-1 SRL factor, conscious motivational strategies, and deep learning techniques were analyzed with WLSMV, followed by a Wu-Estabrook multigroup ordinal invariance sequence a
papers.summary: This study tested whether three dimensions of the GAEU-1 instrument—self-regulated learning, conscious motivational strategies, and deep learning techniques—measure the same constructs equivalently in Chilean and Ecuadorian university students. Using ordinal measurement invariance analysis (WLSMV with a Wu-Estabrook sequence) on 1,316 respondents, the authors assessed whether cross-national comparisons of these learning-regulation constructs are psychometrically justified. The work is a psychometric validation study rather than a biological or bioinformatics contribution.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics and machine learning identify key hub genes in early-onset gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a clinically and biologically distinct subtype of gastric cancer characterized by unique molecular features. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify EOGC-associated hub genes using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning framework.
papers.summary: This study applies an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning pipeline to transcriptomic data from early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) to identify hub genes that may underlie its distinct molecular biology. The work nominates candidate genes for further validation, offering a starting point for understanding EOGC-specific mechanisms.

papers.title: BKPyVN-associated macrophage subpopulations and diagnostic biomarker identification - combine machine learning with single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: As pivotal effector cells of innate immunity, macrophages may play a critical role in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) following kidney transplantation. However, their subpopulation heterogeneity, molecular characteristics, and functional mechanisms remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to characterize macrophage subpopulations in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) after kidney transplantation. The authors identify distinct macrophage populations and propose candidate diagnostic biomarkers, linking macrophage heterogeneity to immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in this disease.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational methods—spanning molecular modeling, network analysis, and systems-level approaches—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these strategies address the stagnation of conventional pipelines amid rising multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains. The paper serves as an overview of computational tooling for TB drug development rather than presenting new experimental findings.

papers.title: Biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting antisense oligonucleotide knockdown efficacy under small-data constraints.
papers.abstract: A central strategy in treating neurodegenerative disorders, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), is lowering levels of disease-driving proteins. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) offer a direct RNA-targeted approach to reduce protein expression, but experimental discovery and optimization are constrained by small, heterogeneous datasets and target-specific variability. Computational models that predict ASO knockdown efficacy directly from sequence and context could improve candidate selection, yet generalization across gene families and experimental settings remains challenging. In t
papers.summary: The authors present a biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting how effectively antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) reduce target protein levels, a key strategy for treating neurodegenerative diseases like ALS. The approach is designed to work with the small, heterogeneous datasets typical of ASO research, aiming to improve candidate selection across different genes and experimental conditions.

papers.title: Identification of SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker for AML and COVID-19 via integrative bioinformatics, machine learning and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA
papers.summary: This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets, machine learning, and Mendelian randomization to identify SLC15A3 as a gene whose expression is shared between acute myeloid leukemia and COVID-19, proposing it as a prognostic biomarker for both conditions. The authors screened 109 common differentially expressed genes and characterized their functions and regulatory networks before narrowing to SLC15A3. The work is exploratory and biomarker-hypothesis-generating rather than a validated clinical finding.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug-food homologous substance target prediction.
papers.abstract: High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug-food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic data and multidimensional bioinformatics to identify candidate genes underlying high-altitude illness, then predicts targets of 106 drug-food homologous substances as potential interventions. It links molecular signatures of altitude response to putative natural compounds, offering hypotheses for prevention or treatment.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing traditional bottlenecks of long timelines, high costs, and inter-patient heterogeneity.

papers.title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the research landscape of cardiac diffusion MRI (cDMRI), a noninvasive technique for probing cardiac microstructure. It characterizes publication trends, key contributors, and thematic clusters in the field, and uses these patterns to project future research directions. The work is a descriptive overview rather than a new methodological or biological finding.

papers.title: QAMQOR: a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition in robot-assisted autism therapy.
papers.abstract: Reliable engagement recognition is important for adaptive robot-assisted autism therapy (RAAT). However, progress remains constrained by the scarcity of publicly available benchmarks evaluated under realistic deployment conditions. Existing studies commonly adopt random train-test splits, which can inflate reported performance because recordings from the same child or therapy session may appear in both the training and test sets. To address this gap, we introduce QAMQOR, a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition collected during RAAT sessions with 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.summary: QAMQOR is a new benchmark dataset for recognizing engagement in children with autism during robot-assisted therapy sessions, collected from 34 children. The authors highlight that existing studies often use random train-test splits that can leak data from the same child or session into both sets, inflating performance, and propose this benchmark to enable more realistic evaluation.

papers.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with ensemble machine learning to identify isonicotinylation-related and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, followed by in vitro validation. The work highlights protein post-translational modification and immune cell dysregulation as contributing mechanisms in DMD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio and improved prognostication of renal cell carcinoma: machine learning-based analysis.
papers.abstract: To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC.
papers.summary: This study introduces the lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR) as a novel prognostic marker for renal cell carcinoma and uses machine learning to evaluate its ability to improve risk stratification. The findings suggest that incorporating LCR into prognostic models may enhance prediction of patient outcomes compared to existing approaches.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approa
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys computational approaches for applying deep learning to EEG analysis, with a focus on diagnosing neurological diseases. It explains how deep learning enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy despite challenges like non-stationarity, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability in EEG signals.

papers.title: Protective effects of testosterone replacement therapy on brain tumor outcomes: The Mayo Clinic experience.
papers.abstract: Biological sex and endocrine signaling influence cancer biology, immune response, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that testosterone signaling may exert brain-context-dependent protective effects in glioblastoma (GBM) through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression, and altered tumor-immune interactions. We assessed whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) exposure was associated with survival in solid tumor central nervous system (CNS) metastases and glioblastoma (GBM, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4), settings in which pos
papers.summary: This Mayo Clinic study examined whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is associated with survival outcomes in patients with glioblastoma and solid tumor CNS metastases. The findings suggest TRT exposure may have protective effects on brain tumor outcomes, potentially through endocrine and immune mechanisms involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. The work adds clinical evidence to the hypothesis that testosterone signaling can influence brain tumor biology in a context-dependent manner.

papers.title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether publicly available LLM chatbots can accurately organize and communicate the mixed evidence base on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI), including its heterogeneous phenotypes and the emerging but limited microbiome evidence. The work tests LLM performance in a clinical niche where evidence is uncertain and not yet actionable, probing their usefulness for evidence synthesis and uncertainty communication.

papers.title: Natural language processing for suicidal behavior detection in short Spanish clinical notes from first-contact interviews.
papers.abstract: Suicide is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by social, cultural, biological, and psychological factors, whose early detection remains challenging. According to the World Health Organization, suicide is the third leading cause of death among individuals aged 15-29 years, representing a major public health concern for young populations worldwide. In first-contact clinical settings, screening opportunities are often constrained by limited time, sparse patient information, and operational workflows. This study evaluates the feasibility of detecting suicidal behavior from short Spanish-langua
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether natural language processing can detect suicidal behavior from short Spanish-language clinical notes collected during first-contact interviews. The work addresses a challenging real-world setting where notes are brief and information is sparse, testing the feasibility of automated screening in a language and context that are underrepresented in NLP research.

papers.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited.
papers.summary: This paper uses a protein language model to design hemoglobin variants with improved stability and oxygen affinity, addressing key limitations in artificial blood substitutes. The work demonstrates how pLM-predicted mutation fitness can be combined with biophysical validation to engineer heme-binding proteins, though the abstract suggests the integration is still being established.

papers.title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.
papers.summary: AIPFusion-Net is a computational framework that predicts anti-inflammatory peptides by combining protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors in an interaction-fusion architecture. This addresses the high cost of experimental identification by offering an accurate in silico screening method for candidate anti-inflammatory peptides.
